headline.title: The power grid is in its worst state of the season
headline.text: More than 310 attacks on energy facilities since the start of November. Scheduled outages in nearly every oblast, and all-day blackouts in parts of the country. Patriot interceptors arrive at about 12 a month, far too few to cover substations.

headline.title: The economy has slipped from slow growth into contraction
headline.text: Q3 GDP fell 0.7% year on year, inflation is rising and the NBU raised its key rate to 16.5%. The main drags are labour shortages and power outages.

headline.title: 2027 is short $32.6bn of external financing
headline.text: The European Commission tables a €45bn loan on 18 November. Its fate depends on confidence in anti-corruption policy, which the Carthage case is now testing.

headline.title: Talks resumed after a nine-month pause
headline.text: Fourth trilateral round in Abu Dhabi. No breakthrough; Donbas is the core dispute. The achievable result is a prisoner exchange of 1,000–1,500 on each side.

headline.title: Strikes on Russian refineries work, but only partly
headline.text: Refining capacity is down about 30%, yet crude exports rose to 3.9m barrels a day and October revenue was 65% higher than a year earlier.

domains.name: Energy
situation: Massive strike on 2–3 November; 12 oblasts without power on 9 November.
Strikes on 11 major substations on 10–11 November.
Scheduled outages in nearly every oblast; capacity caps for industry.
Repairs keep failing because of repeat strikes.
domains.diagnosis: The strikes target substations and distribution nodes rather than generation. With current air defence, repairs cannot outpace repeat strikes. Resilience can only come from decentralisation: many small sources are harder to destroy than a few large nodes.

recs.title: A distributed-generation programme prioritising critical infrastructure
recs.what: Gas-piston units, cogeneration and storage for water utilities, hospitals and district heating
recs.metric: MW of distributed capacity; hours without water and heat
recs.effect: Water, heating and hospitals keep running during grid outages. Expected: hours without water and heat in big cities fall several-fold.

recs.title: A separate request to partners for transformers and autotransformers, not just money
recs.what: Reserve equipment pool in the EU, fast-track logistics
recs.effect: Repairing a damaged substation takes days, not weeks, because the equipment is already in stock.

recs.title: Expand electricity imports from the EU and lift price caps on imports
recs.effect: Imports cover part of the peak-hour deficit: fewer outage hours for people and businesses.

metrics.label: Attacks on energy sites per week

domains.name: Air defence & home front
situation: Patriot: about 12 missiles a month on average, roughly 95% via PURL.
European-funded missiles are delayed. The US denies it; Rubio says a delay is possible.
A licence to produce Patriot missiles in Ukraine is stuck at the Pentagon.
Germany pledged $300m; sale of 500 PAC-3 approved, deliveries will take years.
domains.diagnosis: The bottleneck is the number of interceptors, not the money for them. Russia uses ballistic and manoeuvring missiles exactly where air defence is thin. US deliveries also serve as political leverage over Kyiv during talks.

recs.title: Secure a public PURL delivery schedule with a monthly paid vs delivered reconciliation
recs.what: Through NATO and European payers, not only Washington
recs.effect: A public schedule makes quiet delays impossible, so cover for key sites can be planned months ahead.

recs.title: Scale up cheap interception: interceptor drones, mobile fire teams, electronic warfare
recs.what: Save expensive missiles for ballistic threats
recs.metric: Share of Shaheds downed; cost per intercept
recs.effect: Downing a Shahed costs a fraction as much, and scarce Patriot missiles are kept for ballistic threats. More targets downed on the same budget.

recs.title: Diversify suppliers: SAMP/T, IRIS-T, NASAMS, co-production in Europe
recs.effect: Less dependence on one supplier: a US delay no longer leaves cities undefended.

domains.name: Front line
situation: ISW: no significant advances on most axes (neither side advanced on 9–10 November).
Kostiantynivka: a local ceasefire. ISW assesses Russia is using it to mass forces for a push on Druzhkivka, a fortified node of the Fortress Belt.
Sumy axis: limited attacks, no confirmed advances.
domains.diagnosis: The front is stable, but the lull near Kostiantynivka looks like preparation for an offensive, not de-escalation. Russia pairs negotiations with preparing pressure on Donbas's fortress belt.

recs.title: Treat local lulls with suspicion: keep reserves on the Druzhkivka–Kramatorsk axis
recs.metric: Weekly front-line changes per ISW and DeepState
recs.effect: If the push on Druzhkivka starts, reserves are already in place: lower risk of a breakthrough and of losing a fortified node.

recs.title: A public audit of fortification building: timelines, money, readiness
recs.what: Past scandals over fortification quality make this a trust issue
recs.effect: Fortification money reaches trenches and concrete, and trust in rear-area decisions grows.

domains.name: Military manpower
situation: On 26 October the Rada extended mobilisation for 90 days.
The simplified return after AWOL has ended; the standard procedure through the Military Law Enforcement Service now applies.
Recruitment-centre violations (Ternopil, State Bureau of Investigation), court cases over fines, a new law on fines up to UAH 170,000.
domains.diagnosis: AWOL is a symptom of missing clear terms of service and rotations. Recruitment-centre scandals undermine trust in mobilisation more than enemy propaganda does. Ending the simplified return may reduce the number of soldiers coming back.

recs.title: Clear terms of service and demobilisation, rotations, leave
recs.effect: Clear terms of service cut AWOL and make mobilisation look fairer. Over time, more contract volunteers.

recs.title: Extend or restore the simplified AWOL return with a guaranteed transfer to another unit
recs.effect: Some of those who went AWOL return to service instead of facing prosecution: thousands of soldiers without new mobilisation.

recs.title: Body cameras and a digital trail for all recruitment-centre procedures, with a monthly public violations report
recs.effect: Fewer abuses and scandals; trust in recruitment centres and mobilisation stops falling.

domains.name: Economy
situation: GDP: Q2 +0.4%, Q3 −0.7% y/y. Dragon Capital forecasts −0.5% for 2026.
Inflation is rising (about 11% in October, unconfirmed); the NBU expects 12.5% by year-end.
Key rate 16.5%, which the NBU expects to hold until Q2 2027.
Acute labour shortages in industry, construction and logistics.
The hryvnia is strengthening against the euro and stable against the dollar.
domains.diagnosis: The economy is held back by two constraints: people and electricity. Rate hikes restrain inflation but weigh on credit and growth. The president has few direct levers; the NBU is independent. The main tools go through the Cabinet and the labour market.

recs.title: A Work with a Generator programme: backup-power compensation for SMEs in regions with long outages
recs.metric: Business activity index; vacancies on Work.ua
recs.effect: Small businesses keep working through outages, preserving jobs and tax revenue.

recs.title: Labour market: veteran reintegration, employment of women and people over 60, easier hiring of foreign workers
recs.effect: Labour shortages in industry, construction and logistics ease, giving the economy room to grow.

recs.title: Avoid inflationary decisions (sharp regulated-price hikes) until expectations stabilise
recs.effect: Inflation expectations settle sooner, the NBU can cut rates earlier, and credit gets cheaper.

domains.name: Public finance
situation: External financing need for 2027 is $52.6bn, with $20bn confirmed. The IMF puts the gap at $30–35bn.
The European Commission tables a new €45bn loan backed by the EU budget on 18 November.
Ukraine Facility: a record tranche of nearly €8bn (16 November).
The government wants to claw back UAH 19.2bn in reverse subsidies from 218 communities.
domains.diagnosis: This is the main financial question for the next two months. The loan decision depends on EU member states and on the credibility of reforms. Taking money from communities saves little but costs a lot politically, especially near the front.

recs.title: Aim for approval of the €45bn loan at the December European Council, with targeted outreach to hesitant states
recs.effect: Most of the 2027 gap is closed: military pay, pensions and defence procurement are funded without money printing.

recs.title: Get the 2026–2030 anti-corruption strategy (No. 15230-d) adopted by the end of November
recs.what: The EU ambassador publicly criticises the delay, and it is directly tied to funding
recs.effect: The sceptics' main argument in the EU disappears, improving the odds for the loan and new clusters.

recs.title: Keep reverse subsidies for front-line communities; cut them only for wealthy rear communities
recs.effect: Front-line communities keep money for shelters, water and heat; tension between Kyiv and local government eases.

domains.name: Anti-corruption
situation: The Carthage case (NABU/SAPO): investigators allege a scheme involving SBU, National Police and Prosecutor General's Office officials. An SBU general was released on UAH 65m bail.
The SBU is running an internal review and has dismissed two officials. Media report the Prosecutor General was removed.
NABU's director says the bureau now has too many enemies. Protesters demand reform of the State Bureau of Investigation and an open contest for Prosecutor General.
domains.diagnosis: This tests whether the clash between the authorities and NABU will repeat. Any step that looks like pressure on the bureau would immediately hit EU funding, accession talks and public mood. The strong move is visible support for the investigation.

recs.title: Openly back the investigation and pledge non-interference in NABU and SAPO
recs.effect: Partners and the public see the authorities do not protect insiders; the risk of EU funding being paused falls.

recs.title: An open contest for Prosecutor General with international experts
recs.effect: An independent Prosecutor General raises trust in investigations and lowers the risk of political pressure on cases.

recs.title: Restrict security-service access to Safe City camera systems and log every query
recs.what: Case materials say suspects illegally tracked a car through this system
recs.effect: Surveillance systems stop being a tool for stalking; abuse becomes traceable.

metrics.label: Non-competitive spend in risk topics (by value)

domains.name: Diplomacy
situation: Abu Dhabi, 10–11 November: fourth round of US–Russia–Ukraine talks. Kushner cites progress; no breakthrough.
Russia demands all of Donbas; Ukraine wants a line along the current front.
A prisoner exchange of 1,000–1,500 on each side is under discussion.
Russia opposes European participation in the next round.
EU: clusters 1, 2, 3 and 6 are open. Hungary again blocked clusters 4 and 5 on 10 November.
domains.diagnosis: ISW assesses the Kremlin sees these talks as a way to redraw Europe's security architecture. The risk: the US pushes for concessions on Donbas, using air-defence deliveries as leverage. The public rejects territorial concessions, which strengthens the negotiators' hand.

recs.title: Secure a prisoner exchange as a quick, measurable result of the round
recs.effect: Hundreds or thousands of Ukrainians come home, and the talks deliver a measurable result the public supports.

recs.title: Align with Europe: security guarantees are settled before territorial questions, not after
recs.effect: Ukraine is not left alone under pressure: guarantees become concrete before any concession.

recs.title: Hungary: a bilateral track on minority rights and parallel informal work on clusters 4 and 5
recs.effect: Opening clusters 4 and 5 speeds up EU accession and access to EU funds.

domains.name: Society & demography
situation: KIIS: 62% trust the president (a rally effect amid US pressure); most reject handing over Donbas.
4.38m Ukrainians under temporary protection in the EU until March 2028. Since 31 July new applicants must show they met military obligations.
Refinery strikes: Russian refining −30%, a fuel crisis, tanks burned at Ust-Luga. Crude exports, meanwhile, are rising.
domains.diagnosis: Society is holding, but trust is a resource that mobilisation decisions and corruption scandals use up. Refinery strikes cause a domestic fuel crisis in Russia but do not yet cut its export revenue, because oil is expensive.

recs.title: Use the rise in Russian oil exports to argue for new sanctions on the shadow fleet and export infrastructure
recs.metric: Russian oil exports, bbl/day; IEA revenue
recs.effect: Lower oil revenue means less money for Russia's war, including strikes on Ukraine's grid.

recs.title: Prepare a return programme for 2028: housing, jobs, diploma recognition, tax incentives
recs.effect: Even a partial return of the 4.38m citizens eases labour shortages and demographic losses.

metrics.label: Ukrainians protected in the EU, m

priorities.title: Energy and air defence: NSDC meeting
priorities.text: Decide on a distributed-generation programme for critical infrastructure and mass deployment of cheap interception.

priorities.title: The €45bn EU loan
priorities.text: Call EU leaders after the 18 November proposal. Target approval in December.

priorities.title: Carthage: a public stance
priorities.text: A statement backing NABU, an open contest for Prosecutor General, pressure on the Rada over the anti-corruption strategy.

priorities.title: Talks: prisoner exchange
priorities.text: Lock in a 1,000-for-1,000+ exchange and push for European participation in the next round.

priorities.title: Patriot via PURL
priorities.text: Publicly demand a paid vs delivered reconciliation together with Germany, Norway and Canada.

corruption.lead: Corruption is not a separate area but a tax on all the others. This view shows where it hits hardest, what known cases cost and what the country could have bought with that money.

kpis.label: Recovered and saved
kpis.sub: H1 2026 · incl. UAH 726m saved on drones

cases.title: Midas: kickbacks at Energoatom
cases.detail: Investigators allege contractors were made to pay 10–15% of contract value. Energoatom has still not been recognised as a victim.

cases.title: Kozyn cottage settlement
cases.detail: Suspicion of money laundering against a former head of the President's Office and six others. Guilt not proven in court.

cases.title: Drones for the Defence Forces (State Special Communications)
cases.detail: Prices for DJI Mavic 3 and Autel Evo Max 4T were 60–90% above market; the difference went to controlled firms, including abroad.

cases.title: Substation protection in Kherson oblast
cases.detail: Closed contracts with a firm whose review was done by a state company headed by the founder's brother. Media investigation.

cases.title: Ukroboronprom
cases.detail: Investigators put losses above UAH 32m; about UAH 19m more was prevented.

cases.title: Recruitment-centre and medical-board schemes
cases.detail: In one Kyiv scheme ≥100 men were removed from the register and 31 left the country; organisers' income is put at $60k a month.
cases.stage: Dozens of SBI, SBU and police cases

cases.title: Carthage: SBU, police, Prosecutor General's Office
cases.detail: Investigators allege a criminal group of 12+ people, including an SBU general, with illegal tracking via Safe City cameras.

schemes: Substation protection without tenders and at inflated prices
spheres.without: The Midas case alone (≈ UAH 4.5bn) equals about 50 concrete shelters for 110 kV substations at UAH 90m each. For comparison, all priority substations in Kyiv oblast need UAH 2.3bn. Without corruption, grid protection could have been finished before winter.

schemes: Inflated prices for drones and parts
spheres.without: With a 60–90% markup, every UAH 100 buys UAH 53–63 of real drones. Without corruption the same budget would buy 1.6–1.9 times more equipment. The UAH 254m loss equals about 220 interceptor drones at $25k.

schemes: Fortifications paid for but not built
Inflated prices in the defence industry
spheres.without: Fortifications are built on time and to spec, and troops have prepared positions before an offensive. The room found no 2026 fortification cases.
Mobilisation is seen as fair: it is no longer the people without money who serve. One Kyiv scheme alone removed ≥100 men from the reserve, a whole replacement company.
Honest businesses stop losing to smugglers on price. The budget gains UAH 110–125bn a year, about 8% of the 2027 external financing gap.
Every high-profile case is an argument against aid in EU capitals. Without corruption scandals, the €45bn loan is decided faster and with fewer conditions.
Law enforcement protects the law, not schemes, and NABU cases meet no resistance. Trust in the state, the key wartime resource, stops being wasted.
Hungary and other sceptics find it harder to block clusters on rule-of-law grounds, and Ukraine's negotiating position is stronger.

schemes: Petty corruption in health and education
spheres.without: People see the rules apply to everyone, which raises willingness to bear the war's burdens and refugees' readiness to return.

recs.title: Publish all energy-protection and defence contracts with a 3–6 month delay
recs.effect: Overpricing becomes visible to journalists and auditors; Prozorro's experience suggests openness cuts prices by 10–15%.

recs.title: Mandatory price benchmarks for drones and parts via an e-catalogue
recs.effect: A 60–90% markup becomes impossible; the same budget buys noticeably more drones.

recs.title: Reboot customs: open contest for its head, automated clearance, sanctions on cargo carriers
recs.effect: The Rada inquiry estimates closing schemes adds UAH 15–20bn in the first year and up to UAH 110–125bn over time.

recs.title: Digital mobilisation: random assignment of medical-board doctors, video recording, all decisions only through Oberih with an audit log
recs.metric: Bribery cases in recruitment centres and boards per month
recs.effect: The points where one person can sell another's fate disappear; mobilisation becomes fairer and meets less resistance.

corruption.note: All cases are as reported by investigators and media. A suspicion is not proof of guilt; only a court decides. Conversions into shelters and interceptors illustrate scale and are not precise estimates.
